newsitem.title: CHINA: China sentences "peeping tom" activist to labour.
newsitem.headline: China sentences "peeping tom" activist to labour.

text.p: Chinese police have ordered a former labour activist to serve three years "re-education through labour" for peeping into a women's public toilet, a Hong Kong-based human rights group said on Friday.

Liu Huanwen, 36, arrested on February 24 for the catch-all offence of hooliganism, was ordered on April 7 to serve three years of re-education through labour, Human Rights and Democratic Movement in China said in a statement.

The group described Liu as a former leader of an independent labour union during the 1989 student-led demonstrations for more democracy and said he had been detained for 1-1/2 years after the protests were crushed.

Beijing public security authorities sentenced Liu to the administrative punishment, which does not require a judicial trial, for allegedly peeping into a women's public toilet, the Hong Kong group said, quoting Liu's friends and relatives in Beijing.

Liu, a Christian, had previously been sentenced in July 1994 to two years of re-education through labour for taking part in underground religious activities, the group said. He was released in July last year.

Liu, who according to some accounts has hepatitis, was being held at a police detention centre in eastern Beijing and was expected to be transferred soon to the Tuanhe Labour Farm in the suburbs of the capital, the group said.
Liu's family and Chinese police could not be reached for comment.

In recent years, Chinese authorities have increasingly used the administrative punishment of re-education through labour to silence their critics without going through a complicated trial process. The maximum term is three years.
